Diophantine equations

Source: R/solvers-diophantine.R
diophantine.Rd

diophantine(eq) finds the integer solutions of a polynomial equation with integer coefficients, as a FiniteSet of Tuples ordered like the sorted free symbols (or syms). Parametric families use integer parameters such as t_0, t_1. Linear, binary quadratic (including Pell equations), homogeneous ternary quadratic, general Pythagorean, sums of squares and sums of even powers are supported, and products of such factors. permute = TRUE adds the sign and order permutations SymPy adds. classify_diop(eq) returns the variables, coefficients and type; diop_solve(eq) solves one equation of a known type.

Usage

diophantine(
  eq,
  param = Symbol("t", integer = TRUE),
  syms = NULL,
  permute = FALSE
)

classify_diop(eq)

diop_solve(eq, param = Symbol("t", integer = TRUE))

Arguments

eq

An equation or an expression equal to zero.

param

The base name of the parameters.

syms

Optional order of the variables.

permute

Add sign and order permutations of the solutions.

Value

A set of tuples; classify_diop() returns a list.

Examples

x <- Symbol("x"); y <- Symbol("y"); z <- Symbol("z")
diophantine(2*x + 3*y - 5)
#> {(3*t_0 - 5, 5 - 2*t_0)}
diophantine(x^2 - 2*y^2 - 1)
#> {(-sqrt(2)*(3 - 2*sqrt(2))^t + 3*(3 - 2*sqrt(2))^t/2 + sqrt(2)*(2*sqrt(2) + 3)^t + 3*(2*sqrt(2) + 3)^t/2, -(3 - 2*sqrt(2))^t + 3*sqrt(2)*(3 - 2*sqrt(2))^t/4 - 3*sqrt(2)*(2*sqrt(2) + 3)^t/4 - (2*sqrt(2) + 3)^t), (-3*(3 - 2*sqrt(2))^t/2 + sqrt(2)*(3 - 2*sqrt(2))^t - 3*(2*sqrt(2) + 3)^t/2 - sqrt(2)*(2*sqrt(2) + 3)^t, -3*sqrt(2)*(3 - 2*sqrt(2))^t/4 + (3 - 2*sqrt(2))^t + (2*sqrt(2) + 3)^t + 3*sqrt(2)*(2*sqrt(2) + 3)^t/4)}
diophantine(x^2 + y^2 - z^2)
#> {(2*p*q, p^2 - q^2, p^2 + q^2)}
classify_diop(x^2 + y^2 - x*y + x + 5)
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]][[1]]
#> x
#> 
#> [[1]][[2]]
#> y
#> 
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]]$`x^2`
#> 1
#> 
#> [[2]]$`x*y`
#> -1
#> 
#> [[2]]$x
#> 1
#> 
#> [[2]]$`y^2`
#> 1
#> 
#> [[2]]$`1`
#> 5
#> 
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> [1] "binary_quadratic"
#>
